members.biography:
Ekaterina Matveeva is Director at Amolingua, an edtech company specializing in language learning, cultural intelligence, and multilingual soft skills training using the proprietary Language Alter Ego methodology, and at Lingoplus, an EU co-funded edtech company focused on teacher training. Amolingua is also a running Language Institute at TXST CE. 

Since 2023, Ekaterina has been leading linguistic consulting and prompt development teams for AI companies in Asia, focusing on conversational fluency, cross-cultural sensitivity, and emotionally intelligent responses across 7+ languages. She has also been collaborating with top US AI companies, running RLHF with writer and reviewer teams on education-focused projects, and providing expert feedback on linguistic relevance, pedagogical usefulness, and cultural nuance.
Beyond her technical work, 

Ekaterina has given talks on AI and education, and currently co-organizes roundtables as part of the "Year of AI Challenged" series, bringing together practitioners to grapple openly with the unresolved questions in responsible AI development.

She believes linguistically and culturally attuned AI isn't a luxury feature, it's foundational.

Dr Akbar Husnoo is a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence researcher, educator, and technology professional with expertise spanning AI, data science, cyber resilience, and responsible technology. He holds a PhD in Cybersecurity from Deakin University, where his research focused on AI-driven intrusion detection and resilient critical infrastructure. His experience extends across academia, local government, and industry, with a strong focus on translating emerging technologies into practical, responsible outcomes.

Dr Jelina Haines is a Filipino-born Australian interdisciplinary textile artist, visual designer, researcher, and cultural storyteller. Her work uniquely intersects art, digital technology, information ethics, and cross-cultural community engagement.
Almuyed Saad is an AI policy and data analysis expert from SUST in Bangladesh.

I am a Foreign Affairs Officer at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bangladesh, based in Dhaka. I bring a dual background in software engineering and international relations, holding a BSc in Software Engineering and a Professional Master's in International Relations and Diplomacy. My work sits at the intersection of technology and diplomacy, and I am working toward technology-policy roles within international organizations, with particular interest in adapting AI governance frameworks for developing-country contexts.

Mohsena Akter Drishty is an AI governance researcher and policy analyst based in Bangladesh, with seven years of experience in areas of responsible technology, digital rights, and regulatory analysis. She has conducted country-level AI governance assessments for the Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP) and has been promoted to Team Leader for the Fall 2026 Advanced Clinic cohort. Her earlier work includes producing 250+ legal research outputs for organizations, non-profits, law firms and academics.

She publishes The Harm Index, an independent AI policy publication on Substack covering algorithmic accountability, digital rights, and technology-facilitated harm in South Asia. She also serves as a Founding Board Member for AI Ethics and Standards at Am I Tech Enough Ltd. in Dubai.

Nafiul Ahmad Rafi is an AI governance researcher and policy architect based in Dhaka, Bangladesh, and Founding Director of Atlas AI Institute, a Global South AI governance and policy research initiative. His research examines the governance infrastructure and regulatory capacity needed for responsible AI adoption in developing and emerging economies, with an emphasis on institutional readiness and equitable participation in international norm-setting forums. Through Atlas AI Institute he advances Global South perspectives in multilateral AI governance processes, and his work spans regulatory capacity assessment, comparative Global South AI policy analysis (including country-level AI policy and governance SWOT frameworks), and the link between governance research and digital inclusion and civic technology. He also serves as National AI Policy Endorser at the AI Policy Lab, Umeå University, Sweden, and is a member of the CIVICUS policy network, the Internet Society and the Responsible AI Hub.

Neaz Mujeri is a researcher and AI governance and literacy professional working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, sustainability, systems thinking, and inclusive development. He is Executive Director & CEO of the Center for Research Initiatives (CRI), where he leads research and knowledge initiatives on AI literacy, responsible AI adoption, and sustainable development. His research interests include AI governance, Generative AI, AI literacy and capability-building, sustainability, and the role of AI in advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly in the Global South.

Neaz has academic and research experience across Bangladesh, Canada, the United Arab Emirates, and Australia, including research on Generative AI and sustainability. He has authored and co-authored books and peer-reviewed research and actively contributes to professional and academic discussions on responsible AI and emerging AI governance frameworks. His work is guided by a strong commitment to ensuring that perspectives and priorities from the Global South are meaningfully represented in the development of global AI policy and governance.

I did my PhD from the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Rutgers University, New Jersey. My research works lie at the intersection of Signal Processing, Machine Learning and Wireless Communication. At present I'm focusing on developing machine learning algorithm for Device Free Indoor Localization using WiFi Signals. I have prior research experience in Speech Enhancement using Wavelet Packet Transform. Currently I am focusing my research on developing IoT based healthcare system in Bangladesh

I am looking for motivated and hard working students for Masters and PhD in BUET in the above mentioned area of machine learning, AI and IoT.

Zico Chakma is a Communication and Journalism graduate from the University of Chittagong, Bangladesh, and is currently pursuing his M.S.S. in Communication and Journalism at the same institution. He is a communication professional with a particular focus on Indigenous storytelling, documentary storytelling, and community-centered communication.

As a youth fellow at ICCAD, Zico is engaged in exploring emerging issues at the intersection of communication, technology, and society. His interests extend to the Indigenous and environmental dimensions of AI policy and governance, particularly how emerging technologies can be developed and governed in ways that are inclusive, ethical, and responsive to Indigenous communities and environmental concerns.

Through storytelling, research, and youth engagement, he aims to amplify underrepresented voices and contribute to more inclusive approaches to communication, technology, and policymaking.

I am an AI safety and governance (AIGP) researcher working at the intersection of technology, public interest, and global risks.

My professional background is rooted in infectious disease epidemiology, molecular biology and data science. Previously, I worked at the World Health Organization, where I delivered mission-critical analytics supporting outbreak response in multi-country deployments, enabling rapid institutional decision-making under uncertainty.  I led outbreak analytics during global health emergencies (eg. Go.Data software implementation for contact tracing for Ebola and COVID-19), and pandemic H1N1 influenza, Ebola, plague and COVID-19 outbreaks , across diverse contexts such as the Netherlands, the UK, Madagascar, Guinea, Mali, Laos PDR, Guatemala, the DRC, Fiji, and Moldova. This work required making high-stakes decisions under deep uncertainty, managing complex systems, and anticipating cascading failures, experiences that continue to shape how I approach AI risk.

As AI systems have become increasingly powerful and socially embedded, my focus has shifted toward AI safety, governance, and policy, particularly where failures could have large-scale or irreversible consequences. I work on issues including AI risk governance, algorithmic accountability and auditing, and the design of institutional and policy frameworks capable of responding to rapidly advancing technologies. I am currently working at the EU AI office on AI Safety. The European AI Office supports the development and adoption of trustworthy Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions, while protecting people against risks.

Sithar Norbu is a Chief Program Officer with the Public Service Delivery Division, Prime Minister’s Office, Royal Government of Bhutan. His work focuses on simplifying and standardizing government services, improving citizen journeys, strengthening inter-agency coordination, and expanding integrated service channels for citizens and businesses.

He holds an International Master’s in Artificial Intelligence for Public Services from Universidad Politécnica de Madrid and a Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Computer Science from the University of Delhi. His professional interests include citizen-centred digital government, GovTech, service design, digital inclusion, responsible AI and data governance.

I hold an MSc in Digital Society at the University of Edinburgh under the Chevening Award, a postgraduate degree in Business Administration from FGV, and a degree in International Relations. I currently work as a Project Management Consultant for the UK Government’s Digital Access Programme (DAP), supporting the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). In this role, I manage projects focused on digital technologies, artificial intelligence, digital policy, digital safety, and meaningful connectivity.

Throughout my career, I have worked with several international organisations and leading institutions, including the University of Cambridge, Microsoft, The Ohio State University, and Facebook (now Meta). At Meta, I served as a Programme Manager.

At Microsoft, I also served as the leader of BAM in Brazil, and Business Manager for the External and Corporate Affairs department connecting digital technology and policy. At Microsft I developed strategies and initiatives aimed at creating a more diverse and inclusive environment within the technology sector. My work focused on professional development, self-awareness, networking, and advancing discussions on racial equity in Brazil. I also created initiatives to raise awareness of digital exclusion in Brazil.

As a consultant to the British Government’s Digital Access Programme, I have managed several projects focused on the intersection of technology, public policy, and social impact. One example is the “Digital Technologies and Environmental Sustainability in Brazil” project, which focused on mapping and disseminating research on the use of artificial intelligence to support environmental sustainability while addressing and mitigating the risks associated with its adoption. 

Another example is a Digital Citizenship project implemented in collaboration with SaferNet and Brazil’s Ministry of Education. I played an instrumental role in designing and implementing digital safety and citizenship courses that reached 145,548 students across 1,065 schools in all 27 Brazilian states. I co-wrote the project proposal, managed its implementation, and ensured alignment with both Brazilian and UK Government priorities. By supporting the integration of digital safety initiatives into public policy, I contributed to significant nationwide impact, demonstrating my ability to manage large-scale projects and navigate complex international collaborations.

International Relations undergraduate student at the Federal University of Goiás (UFG) and Researcher at the Center of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence (CEIA)—Latin America's largest AI research center—where she develops the "CEIA AI Policy & Governance Lab" project, investigating digital sovereignty, international security, and global AI governance. First winner of the 1st Mônica de Menezes Campos Award by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil and Project Leader for the Government of the State of Goiás, she works strategically at the intersection of technology, foreign policy, and innovation.

I am a Brazilian social impact and innovation professional with more than 25 years of experience working at the intersection of socio-environmental development, inclusion, institutional transformation and, increasingly, artificial intelligence, in Brazil and in some African countries.
I am the co-founder of SUL – Inteligência para Impacto, a Brazil-based impact tech focused on developing and applying AI to social and environmental challenges in the Global South. My work combines AI literacy, responsible AI adoption, knowledge development and the design of AI solutions for organizations and communities working in contexts of social and economic inequality.
Through SUL, I co-lead the development of Mariah, an AI-based educational and business support platform designed to expand access to knowledge, capabilities and decision support for nano and microentrepreneurs, particularly those underserved by conventional technology and business support systems. Mariah combines education, conversational AI and practical business support to make technology more accessible and useful in everyday economic life.
We are also developing the AI Brain for Impact, a knowledge infrastructure designed to organize and connect curated knowledge, support knowledge management and enable collaborative knowledge creation across the social impact ecosystem. The goal is not simply to make information searchable, but to create an intelligent layer through which people and organizations can access, connect, interpret and collectively develop knowledge for action.
My work is grounded in the belief that responsible AI in the Global South must go beyond principles and regulation to address questions of access, agency, capacity, inclusion and real-world impact. I hold a Master's degree in International Relations and Development Studies and MBAs in Entrepreneurship & Business Management and Human Resources Development.

I am an AI governance and information security professional and a PhD candidate in Business Administration at UNIVALI, Brazil. My work bridges research and practice, focusing on responsible AI governance, trustworthy AI, human agency, and the societal impacts of generative AI. I was a Visiting PhD Scholar at Bentley University, where I conducted research at the intersection of AI, strategy, governance, and society. I currently work on translating AI governance principles and international frameworks into organizational practices in Brazil.

Ph.D. Candidate in Sustainability Education at Prescott College, NSF Research Fellow, and accredited Independent International Expert (OMEI Geneva N°2688). Expert Contributor to the ITU-T Focus Group on AI for Smart Cities (FG-AI4SSC) and Africa AI Policy Fellow. Co-author of the Africa AI Governance Index 2026, specializing in AI-enabled resilience of critical infrastructure, cybersecurity governance, and digital sustainability across the Global South.

Soumana Dama is a software engineer and AI practitioner from Burkina Faso, currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Emerging Networks, IoT and Embedded Intelligence at Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo. His work spans artificial intelligence, machine learning, NLP, multilingual AI for low-resource African languages, computer vision, and agentic AI systems.

He is the Founder & Lead AI Engineer of Scoinvestigator AI, a multi-agent scientific research assistant designed to help researchers explore scientific literature, synthesize evidence, and reason across complex information. He has also developed AI technologies for Mooré and Dioula and applied AI solutions in areas including agriculture and sustainable development.

Through building and deploying AI systems, he has developed a strong interest in AI governance, responsible AI, AI reliability, and the challenges of developing and deploying AI in low-resource contexts. He is particularly interested in ensuring that AI governance reflects the realities, priorities, and technological needs of the Global South.

I am an epidemiologist and field researcher with 13+ years of experience in rigorous research, evidence generation, data analysis, and international programs, now transitionning his career to AI governance. I coordinated the deployment of a machine learning diagnostic tool for cervical cancer screening in Malawi, an experience that exposed significant gaps in AI oversight and regulation across under-resourced health systems in Africa.

I am the author of IA & Cadres Dirigeants (IACD), an AI governance newsletter for executives, CEOs, and decision-makers in the public and private sectors, which has grown to nearly 6,000 subscribers on LinkedIn. I am currently completing a pedagogical book on AI risks for the general public, aimed at improving AI literacy in francophone Africa. My work focuses on closing the AI governance and literacy gap in francophone and under-resourced regions of the Global South, combining a research background in data ethics and regulatory compliance with a commitment to making AI risk understandable and actionable for non-technical audiences.

I am a passionate advocate of sustainable science, transformative and resilient mindsets for a thriving and impactful Africa. I hold a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Bremen, Germany, and currently serves as an Associate Professor at the University of Ngaoundere in Cameroon. With over 20 years of expertise in digital transformation, cybersecurity and data intelligence, I am the founder and Chair of the Cybersecurity with Computational and Artificial Intelligence Group. Recently, I was appointed Technical Advisor and Consultant Professor at the School of Engineering Science and Technology of Kesmonds International University (KIU). With more than 30 publications including papers, conferences and books, and several certifications in Digital Transformation, AI Strategy & Governance, and Cybersecurity Management, I am a globally recognized scientist with significant contributions to the fields of cybersecurity and AI. 
I am an active member of several national and international professional societies, and recipient of numerous awards, recognitions, fellowships, and research grants for my work. I co-invented platforms such as eyeandears.com, an AI-powered platform for combating misinformation, and the Cybersecurity Academy app, which educates users of all ages in digital safety.
Dedicated to youth empowerment and resilience, I recently launched the ResilientMinds initiative, which fosters leadership and personal growth among youth in underprivileged communities. He is also a pioneer of responsible AI in Cameroon. I Founded the International Conference on Safe, Secure, Ethical, and Responsible Technologies and Emerging Applications, and represents Cameroon in the Responsible AI Network–Africa. As a digital transformation expert for the Regional Conference of Rectors of Central African and Great Lakes Universities, he advises on the responsible integration of generative AI in education.
I co-edited the book Global Perspectives on the Applications of Computer Vision in Cybersecurity and contributed to the ICESCO Charter on AI Ethics. He is the Principal Investigator of a three-years U.S.-funded project by DEVCOM ARL and ONR Global, focused on training young African researchers in AI and cybersecurity using Game Theory and Machine Learning.
As the AI ChangeMaker Awardee in 2025 in Cameroon, I continue to champion youth innovation, serving as a keynote speaker with my unceasing to unwavering my commitment is to support Africans life, elevate African research and empower the next generation of change-makers.

I am a computer scientist and AI researcher from Cameroon. My work sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, language, and the realities of communities that are often poorly represented in technology.

I became interested in these questions through research rather than policy. Working on multilingual NLP and AI safety, I have seen how an AI system can behave differently depending on the language, cultural context, and people represented in a prompt. That experience pushed me beyond the question of whether an AI system works, toward a harder question: **works for whom, and according to whose assumptions?**

My research has included building multilingual datasets and studying how large language models respond to culturally grounded information. I am particularly interested in what these findings mean for AI governance in Africa, where policy is often developing alongside technologies that were not designed with African languages, institutions, or social realities in mind.

I want my work to help ensure that Africa is not simply a market, testing ground, or case study for AI, but a place where ideas about how AI should be built and governed are also being developed.

​Citlalli Rios is the President of Hispanotech, where she champions community leadership, professional mentorship, and cross-sector collaboration between industry and academia to drive inclusive innovation. Alongside her professional work at Techmien, she is deeply focused on the intersection of ethical technology and organizational leadership. Having completed the Rotman School of Management's Generative AI for Business course, as well as the Advancing Women's Leadership and Women in Power programs, her core focus centers on AI ethics, technology governance, and building practical accountability frameworks for small businesses.

Governance and Risk Management leader with 15+ years designing and scaling enterprise AI, Cloud, and IT risk governance
frameworks across Tier-1 Canadian financial institutions. Currently leads AI Risk Governance for RBC AI Group, reporting to
the VP, and directing a team of 4 governance managers across the full AI lifecycle. Builds and operationalizes technical
governance controls for model registry and inventory management, model observability and monitoring, risk classification,
and auditability, and establishes Responsible AI standards spanning bias mitigation, transparency, explainability, and human
oversight. Trusted advisor to Legal, Privacy, Risk, and Compliance on regulatory-aligned AI governance operating models
across LLM gateways, Agentic AI, and MCP-server platforms. Holds CISSP, CRISC, CCSK, CBCP, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer,
and ISO 22301 Lead Auditor certifications.

I am an interdisciplinary scholar with work rooted in understanding human behaviour and decision-making that influence health outcomes. My interests lie at the intersection of behavioural science, public health, and emerging technologies with a priority on how algorithmic decision-making interacts with human decision-making in healthcare systems to impact patient care.

Elizabeth Ballesteros is the founder of IGM Human Systems, an emerging research and innovation initiative examining how artificial intelligence affects the formation, exercise and preservation of human capabilities. Her work focuses particularly on human agency, judgment, responsibility and self-trust—and on the developmental environments through which these capacities are built over time.
IGM is developing a human capability framework, research architecture and applied assessment approaches intended to help education systems, organizations and policymakers distinguish between AI-assisted performance and independently possessed human capability. Elizabeth’s wider interests include human development, equitable access to developmental opportunity and the design of human-development-centred AI systems and institutions.

Steven Guerrero is a Costa Rican AI policy and digital governance practitioner working at the intersection of responsible AI, digital transformation, public policy and socioeconomic development. He serves as Vice President of FAIR Costa Rica and has contributed to AI governance research through the Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP), including work on the AI and Democratic Values Index. He is also an adjunct professor at Universidad CENFOTEC and Executive Director of TéiKiq, a digital innovation cluster that brings together government, academia and the private sector. His current interests include AI governance in Latin America, digital strategic autonomy, digital public infrastructure, institutional capacity and development-oriented approaches to emerging technologies.

Scientist, programmer, and entrepreneur in artificial intelligence. Director of AI Safety Dominicana and NeurIPS 2026 reviewer, with experience developing AI solutions and conducting research on AI safety.

Gabriel Hidalgo Andrade is a political scientist, constitutional lawyer, and university professor based in Quito, Ecuador, specializing in political power, governance, and institutional conflict in Latin America. With over 15 years of undergraduate and graduate teaching experience, his research and teaching focus on applied political science, Latin American presidentialism, political elites, and institutional stability. He runs professional training programs in political analysis and public governance for public-sector officials and advisors, and is a regular commentator in national and international media. In 2026, he co-founded E3I (Escenarios · Información · Incidencia · Inteligencia Estratégica), a strategic intelligence organization producing political risk analysis across Ecuador and the region.

I am an Ecuadorian lawyer working at the intersection of public law and the governance of automated decision-making inside public institutions. I hold an LL.M. in International Legal Studies from Georgetown University Law Center, which I completed as a Fulbright Scholar, and a Master's in International Litigation and Arbitration from Universidad San Francisco de Quito. For close to a decade I have worked on the State side of international dispute resolution and constitutional adjudication. At Ecuador's Attorney General's Office I defended the State in investment treaty and commercial arbitrations. At the Constitutional Court of Ecuador I drafted orders, opinions and judgments in constitutional control proceedings, and designed and validated the 128-rule detection set behind the Court's automated case-classification and prioritization system, validated against 40% of first-quarter 2026 case intake and built with an explicit human-review tier so that the routing decision remains human by design.
I works in Spanish and English and I'm interested in how justice-sector institutions in Latin America adopt AI under real capacity constraints.

Yalilé Loaiza is an investigative journalist based in Quito, Ecuador, with over 15 years of experience in journalism and media innovation. She is Editor-in-Chief of Ecuador Chequea, the only fact-checking organization in Ecuador that is a signatory to the IFCN Code of Principles , and leads ChequeaLab, its digital innovation arm developing AI-assisted verification tools. She also serves as President of Fundamedios, Ecuador's leading press freedom organization, and is the Ecuador correspondent for Infobae since 2021. In 2025, she co-founded E3I (Escenarios · Información · Incidencia · Inteligencia Estratégica), a strategic intelligence organization producing political risk analysis and training journalists across Ecuador. She holds a Summa Cum Laude master's degree in Digital Communication Research from Universidad de Los Hemisferios.

Ramy M. Magdi is an economist and a former diplomat. He has more than 15 years of research and management experience at the Bibliotheca Alexandrina (Egypt) as librarian and Director of the Library’s Arabic & Islamic Manuscripts Centre, and later at the Arab League Educational, Cultural & Scientific Organization (ALECSO) (Tunisia) as Chief of Staff and Head of Strategy. He lived in Egypt, Tunisia and the UK and travelled across the Middle East and Europe. 
Ramy engaged in top intergovernmental policy initiatives in the fields of education, research, cultural preservation and counter-terrorism in the MENA region. He took part in collaborative initiatives and projects led by, inter alia, the World Bank, UNESCO, UNICEF and ICESCO. He edited two books on Arabic and Islamic Heritage (published by the Library of Alexandria), organised 16 international conferences and high-level symposia, in addition to 4 international book fairs (2 in Egypt, 1 in Frankfurt and another in London) and helped fundraise and manage USD 2,6000,000 for the benefit of the institutions he worked for.
Ramy studied at University College London (UCL) and graduated with an MSc in International Public Policy with a focus on international political economy, financial inclusion and economic global governance. He also studied English language and civilization and has a BA and another MA in English Language and Natural Language Processing from the University of Alexandria.

I am Dr.Belay Enyew Chekol and an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at the University of Gondar, Ethiopia, specializing in Fuzzy Logic Systems, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data and Web Mining and Intelligent Systems. I have a PhD in Computer Science from Sudan University of Science and Technology, an MCA from Osmania University, India, and a BSc in Library and Information Science from Addis Ababa University.
I have extensive experience in university teaching, postgraduate supervision, academic program coordination, curriculum development, research, and community engagement. He has served as Postgraduate Programs Coordinator in the College of Informatics and previously as Head of the Department of Information Technology at the University of Gondar.
My research interests focus on the application of AI and machine learning to real-world challenges, including disease prediction, intelligent systems, data mining, fuzzy logic, deep learning, digital transformation, and AI-enabled decision support. My research includes work on malaria epidemic prediction, agricultural disease detection, medical image analysis, and AI-related security and governance.
I am particularly interested in advancing responsible, practical, and context-aware AI solutions for developing countries, with an emphasis on translating AI research into applications that can contribute to health, agriculture, public services, education, and sustainable development.

At present, I am a doctoral researcher at Turku School of Economics at the University of Turku working on the topic of AI governance. I have 5 years of research experience both in academia as project and doctoral researcher and industry as a consultant. My current engagement allowed me to invest my intellectual capacity in raising concerns on AI risks and subsequently ensure safety through conducting research and proposing policies and governance mechanisms targeted at organisations as well to respective countries.

I lead the research on AI governance, geopolitics, and geoeconomics at the German Institute for Global and Area Studies (GIGA) in Hamburg. I conduct transdisciplinary projects on impact of AI on political pluralism, communication, and participation in South and Southeast Asia with civil society partners and research institutes from the region and we work to create academic, policy, and socially-consequential articles, policy papers, databases, and networks. I am very interested to join the Coalition as it fully aligns with the work I do and I would like to collaborate with and contribute to the Coalition for cross-learnings, as well as creating and cementing avenues for joint research and policy publications, projects, and networks.

Carl Sherson Clermont is a Haitian digital transformation leader, AI policy and governance practitioner, and CEO & Principal Consultant of CompuConsult. With over two decades of experience at the intersection of technology, public policy, and international development, his work focuses on responsible AI, digital government, digital public infrastructure, cybersecurity, and inclusive innovation. He leads initiatives including SMARTSCHOOL and MÈT-DESCH, a Trusted Educational AI Agent designed to expand responsible and equitable access to AI-powered learning. Carl contributes to regional dialogue on AI governance and digital transformation across Latin America and the Caribbean, with a particular interest in ensuring that Haiti, Small Island Developing States, and other Global South countries actively shape the policies, safeguards, and institutions governing AI.
Co-founder or AI Safety HK, which is HK’s first dedicated organisation on AI safety. I am also an AI governance researcher, and a qualified lawyer with multijurisdictional experience.

Gábor Soós, PhD, is an AI Innovation Strategic Advisor and former Secretary-General of the Hungarian National Commission for UNESCO. He works at the intersection of AI, philosophy, education, culture, sustainability and international cooperation, drawing on more than two decades across UNESCO, public policy, heritage governance, community participation and international programmes.

His recent work asks how societies, communities and places can take part in shaping the intelligence we build. Three questions guide it: how AI can become place-shaped and culture-shaped; how education can move people from access to agency; and how AI can support sustainability and resilience across the source-to-sea continuum while keeping responsibility visible, traceable, local and reversible. These questions inform his work on World-Shaped, Place-Shaped and Culture-Shaped AI, cognitive sovereignty, analogue-first learning, semantic world modelling, Chrono-TOLMA and the Bartók 4.0 learning cycle.

He is Initiator and Lead Coordinator of Source2Sea: Bartók 3.0 Connectivity (a UN Ocean Decade project), Visiting Research Fellow at UNU-CRIS, and Initiator and Steward of the World-Shaped AI Coalition (WOSAIC). In these roles he develops and convenes cross-sector initiatives with universities, UNESCO-related networks, public institutions, local communities, educators and technology partners, with the aim of making relations more visible, uncertainty more legible, provenance more traceable and correction always possible. He is a researcher, author, educator, international speaker and programme initiator.

I want to join the Global South AI Policy Coalition to contribute a practitioner’s perspective to the evolving conversation around responsible AI governance. My work in AI, GenAI, data, and knowledge systems gives me a strong interest in how emerging technologies can be developed and deployed responsibly. I am particularly interested in AI accountability, data governance, and the governance challenges created by agentic AI. The Coalition’s focus on cross-regional collaboration and evidence-based policy strongly aligns with my interests. I would also value the opportunity to learn from and collaborate with researchers, policymakers, and technology practitioners across the Global South.

Currently Im pursuing my DPhil in AI and Journalism focusing integration of AI in Journalism and changing landscape of media ethics and the need of regulatory guidelines in the newsroom from Department of Mass Communication, Rajiv Gandhi (Central) University, Arunachal Pradesh, India. My primary interest span from ethical AI to governance in the field of AI.

Chirag J Belani is an English stenographer, columnist and PA to the Registrar at Atmiya University, Rajkot. He takes accurate dictation and types documents, verbal discussions, letters and passages of every kind, and continues to build on these skills for his professional growth.
A seasoned educator in AI and Data Science. I bring to the table creativity, balanced decision making and effective implementation.

Postgraduate student in Public Policy and Law at Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Hyderabad and Mumbai, with academic and practical exposure to policy research, governance and regulatory analysis. Skilled in quantitative data analysis, large national dataset analysis (NSSO, NFHS, PLFS, HCES, Census) and impact evaluation, with experience in research, fieldwork and policy analysis. Interested in contributing to AI governance and technology policy through evidence-based research, analysis and implementation.

Ishika Rajveer is a development professional with experience across programme management, partnerships, research, knowledge management and strategic communications, working on climate resilience programmes, sustainable housing and social impact initiatives. Her academic background spans Sociology, Public Health and Urban Environmental Management & Law, giving her an interdisciplinary perspective on questions of society, policy, institutions and development. She is increasingly interested in AI governance, responsible AI, digital rights, human agency and the social and regulatory implications of AI, particularly in India and the Global South.

International Relations professional with experience in higher education internationalisation, institutional partnerships and cross-border collaboration. Currently serving as International Relations Officer at the Indian Institute of Management Jammu. My interests include the intersection of emerging technologies, public policy, education and international cooperation, particularly how Global South perspectives can contribute to more inclusive and responsible approaches to AI governance.

16 years of government , mangement consultant
In latest emerging tech.

Japmandeep Singh Ahluwalia, known as Sunny, is an AI governance practitioner based in Gurgaon, India and the founder of Luxyn Ethics and Governance. His work focuses on the gritty operational side of AI safety, specifically accountability triggers, which are hard system checkpoints that force human review before high risk AI decisions are executed. He holds an Oxford University AI Ethics certification and the BSI ISO 42001 Lead Implementer designation, with recent publications on verifiable governance frameworks and the 2026 audit landscape.

He is currently building an EU AI Act Classification Simulator to help organisations operationalise compliance across jurisdictions. He wants to join the Coalition to test this framework against the regulatory realities of the Global South, share practical implementation blueprints, and learn from peers facing the same infrastructure and capacity constraints that define the region's AI trajectory. His focus is always on what works on the ground, not just what looks good in a policy paper.

Megha Gautam is an IP and technology lawyer with an LLM in Intellectual Property, Technology and Information Law from the University of Cambridge. She has practiced on IP drafting, prosecution, and litigation, and is currently co-founding a law firm focused on the intersection of IP, technology, and digital innovation. Her interests include AI governance, algorithmic accountability, and the legal frameworks needed to regulate emerging technologies, particularly in the context of the Global South.
A writer, developer, community builder and researcher working on to lay the frameworks for the governance of Physical and Edge AI.

I am a researcher and Assistant Professor of Geography at Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University, Uttarakhand, India. My work focuses on population geography, spatial demography, health, elections, and the use of geospatial technologies and GeoAI for evidence-based research and public decision-making. I am particularly interested in how AI can be applied responsibly to address real-world challenges in communities across the Global South.

Through my research, teaching, and open mapping initiatives, I work at the intersection of geography, data, technology, and society. I am keen to contribute to the Atlas Global South AI Policy Coalition by sharing perspectives from India, learning from researchers and practitioners across the Global South, and supporting inclusive, ethical, and context-sensitive approaches to AI governance.

Nikunj Doshi is an AI researcher, technology professional, public speaker, and advocate working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, technology policy, and AI governance. He has contributed to the Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP), engaging with issues surrounding responsible AI, AI policy, digital rights, and governance. Sharon Juwah is an AI governance specialist who centres her work on a fundamental question: when an AI system acts inside an institution, who is held liable, and is there a capacity to assess?
